entry: maintainers' floor: Plonky3 uni-STARK at a21f9e38, blake2s-chain-v0 at n = 16384, BabyBear with degree-5 extension challenges, 107 queries at rate 1/4, unique-decoding regime

claims.bounds: probability that FRI accepts a word far from the Reed-Solomon code
claims.source: unique-decoding FRI soundness for Reed-Solomon codes (BCIKS20, eprint 2020/654); folding by up to 8 as in Plonky3's TwoAdicFriPcs

claims.bounds: grinding cost before the query positions are drawn
claims.source: proof-of-work credit in the random-oracle model; query_proof_of_work_bits = 26

claims.bounds: Keccak-256 collisions anywhere in the transcript or the commitments
an adversary opens a Merkle commitment to two different values
claims.derivation: binding reduces to a Keccak-256 collision

claims.bounds: the quotient identity holds at the random out-of-domain point although it fails as polynomials
claims.derivation: constraint degree 3 over 2^14 rows, |F| = |BabyBear^5| ~ 2^155; unique decoding, one candidate codeword

claims.bounds: a far quotient survives the random combination of every opened quotient by powers of one challenge
claims.derivation: (M - 1) |D| / |F| with M = 12186 (the 11920 trace columns at zeta, the 256 message columns at g zeta, 10 quotient columns), |D| = 2^16, |F| ~ 2^155: about 2^-125.4
claims.source: BCIKS20 (eprint 2020/654), correlated agreement for low-degree curves, unique decoding

claims.bounds: a far word survives a FRI fold of up to 8 values with powers of one challenge
claims.derivation: per round (arity - 1) |D_i| / |F| <= 7 |D_i| / |F|, summed over rounds of 2^16, 2^13, ..., 2^1: about 2^-136
claims.source: BCIKS20 (eprint 2020/654), correlated agreement for low-degree curves

claims.bounds: the random combination of the constraints hides a violated one
claims.derivation: about 2^15 constraints combined by powers of one challenge, (C - 1) / |F| ~ 2^-140; no lookup argument. Separately, a reviewer must check that the constraints encode BLAKE2s-256 and the chain exactly; that check is not a number
a single proof of the chain; no inner proof is verified
